card.name: Linking words before symptom mentions
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as you, they, an, new, or a comma, placed just before a symptom or condition is expected, such as in symptom questions or advice to report symptoms.

modes.label: Pronoun before symptoms
modes.description: A pronoun like they or you right before the text says patients experience or have symptoms.
modes.example: advise them to contact a healthcare provider if<< they>> occur.

modes.label: Slot in a list of conditions
modes.description: A comma or adjective inside a list of illnesses or conditions, where another condition name comes next.

modes.label: Symptom questions
modes.description: Words in a symptom-checking question series that ask what else the person feels.
modes.example: What other symptoms do<< you>> have

card.writes: It nudges the output away from the word pain and symptom words, and toward words about intensity and attacks.
card.plain: It fires on small words just before a symptom is named, as if the text is about to say what the patient feels.
